item.content:encoded:
Beijing accused of expanding pressure campaign against Taiwan media and entertainers Beijing is expanding its pressure campaign against Taiwanese entertainers and media figures, using political warnings and access to the Chinese market as leverage, according to Taiwan national security officials, as reported by The Taipei Times. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 19:35 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 19:35 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Beijing is expanding its pressure campaign against Taiwanese entertainers and media figures, using political warnings and access to the Chinese market as leverage, according to Taiwan national security officials, as reported by The Taipei Times. The latest incident involved television host Kevin Tsai, who attended the opening of Democratic Progressive Party Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen’s campaign headquarters. According to The Taipei Times, the Chinese military-affiliated social media account Junzhengping criticised Tsai after his appearance at the event, accusing him of benefiting from the Chinese market while supporting Taiwan independence. The account warned that the Taiwan independence issue was a matter of principle and that there was no room for ambiguity. Taiwanese officials said the move was unusual because Junzhengping has traditionally focused on People’s Liberation Army military exercises and cross-Strait military issues. According to The Taipei Times, officials viewed the criticism as an attempt to establish political boundaries for Taiwanese public figures who have professional or commercial links with China. Tsai had reportedly said that he attended the event to observe the campaign and hear different perspectives, rather than to publicly endorse Shen. The pressure also extended to Taiwan’s media industry. A Chinese media account, Haixia Fengdu, reportedly criticised ETtoday on Douyin, accusing the outlet of supporting Shen and other Democratic Progressive Party politicians. The account also highlighted ETtoday founder Gary Wang’s visits to China and his participation in cross-Strait exchanges before calling for changes to the organization’s editorial staff. The Taipei Times reported that Taiwanese officials believe the two incidents indicate an effort by Beijing to use commercial interests and access to the Chinese market to influence Taiwanese entertainers, businesses and media organisations. Officials warned that such pressure could also be intended to interfere in Taiwan’s elections and restrict freedom of expression. They urged Taiwanese citizens not to be intimidated by political threats or red lines imposed by Beijing. Separately, the National Police Agency said authorities are taking seriously any attempt by foreign forces to interfere in Taiwan’s democratic system or threaten personal safety and freedom of expression. (ANI)

item.title: Iran’s Araghchi says Tehran to respond to US peace plan within days as Pentagon prepares fresh strikes
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said that Tehran will respond to a US peace proposal on the West Asia conflict “within the next few days” amid reports suggesting that ...
item.content:encoded:
Iran’s Araghchi says Tehran to respond to US peace plan within days as Pentagon prepares fresh strikes Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said that Tehran will respond to a US peace proposal on the West Asia conflict “within the next few days” amid reports suggesting that Washington is preparing for military options for a possible resumption of major combat operations against the Islamic Republic. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 18:55 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 18:55 IST

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said that Tehran will respond to a US peace proposal on the West Asia conflict “within the next few days” amid reports suggesting that Washington is preparing for military options for a possible resumption of major combat operations against the Islamic Republic. Speaking after attending an event here, Araghchi said negotiations between Tehran and Washington remain ongoing, with messages continuing to be exchanged through mediators. “The negotiation process is still ongoing and messages are being exchanged through mediators,” Araghchi said, as quoted by Iranian state media, Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB). He stated that Tehran had already presented its proposal, referring to the “Seven-Day Plan”, last month and had received Washington's views on it. “We presented our plan, which we had presented under the title "Seven-Day Plan," and we also heard the American side's views on it,” Araghchi said. “We are currently reviewing the views of the Americans and I think we will provide our response within the next few days,” he added. His remarks came hours after an Axios report stating that US President Donald Trump has not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations against the Islamic Republic; however, the Pentagon has been instructed to prepare for possible fresh strikes. According to Axios, citing US officials, the Pentagon instructed US Central Command (US CENTCOM) several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran. The directive did not set a specific date for launching strikes. US and Israeli officials told Axios that renewed combat operations could take place before the US midterm elections, scheduled to be held on November 3, and possibly ahead of Israeli elections, which are expected a week earlier. If major combat operations resume, they are expected to include extensive strikes on Iranian energy, infrastructure and nuclear targets, Axios reported, citing sources. “The Department's job is to develop and present military options to the President,” a Pentagon official told Axios. A White House official said Trump has all options available at any time. “The U.S. is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz and the Iranian economy collapsing. Iran has been decimated, and things will go one of two ways: the easy way or the hard way,” the official told Axios. “President Trump holds all the cards and will do whatever is best for the United States,” the official added. Last month, during the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), Araghchi presented a proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz under a seven-day plan. Araghchi had said the timeline for the proposed plan would begin once the United States accepted it. According to Al Jazeera, he said Washington would need to take certain actions under the plan, which could be completed within four to five days. “If they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow,” Araghchi said. He said the required steps were already part of a memorandum of understanding and would not be difficult to implement. If the US fulfilled the conditions, he said, the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened on the sixth day, followed by renewed talks between Tehran and Washington on the seventh day. However, Trump had earlier rejected the proposed, as reported by the Wall Street Journal. According to Axios, negotiations between the US and Iran have made no progress, while Qatari mediators are still waiting for an Iranian response to a US counterproposal that included demands for nuclear concessions. “The discussion about possible resumption of major combat operations in Iran has increased. The chances of it happening before the elections is not high but we don't rule it out. After the midterms the chances of it happening increase significantly,” a second Israeli official told Axios. Axios also reported that Trump's national security team met at Camp David on Friday for several hours to discuss the war and other issues. An Israeli official said part of the meeting focused on a possible resumption of major combat operations in Iran. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said after the meeting that it focused on “long-term” foreign policy planning. Trump on Wednesday spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, marking their second call in a few days after they had barely spoken for several weeks. A US official said Trump and Netanyahu spoke about “remembrance and respect for the victims of the October 7 massacre.” The call came after Netanyahu held a meeting with his national security team on Iran, according to the first Israeli official cited by Axios. Netanyahu also spoke with Rubio on Monday. If major combat operations resume, they are likely to involve the US and Israel working in tandem, with the Israeli military participating, according to the report. The two Israeli officials said the Iranian regime is desperate and paranoid, which could lead Tehran to strike first. They said Iran has suffered two surprise attacks and does not want to experience a third. A renewed war could also affect Israeli elections, as Iran would likely fire hundreds of ballistic missiles at Israel in retaliation, Axios reported. Trump had, earlier, told aides he expected to resume bombing Iran after the November midterm elections. This followed Trump's open threat of annihilating Iran during his speech to the UNGA. (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan’s PIMS faces pressure as medicine supplies threatened by procurement delays
item.description: Pakistan’s Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) is facing significant pressure as essential medicine supplies are threatened by ongoing procurement delays, raising concerns over patient care.
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan’s PIMS faces pressure as medicine supplies threatened by procurement delays Pakistan’s Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) is facing significant pressure as essential medicine supplies are threatened by ongoing procurement delays, raising concerns over patient care. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 14:57 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 14:57 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pakistan’s largest public-sector hospital, the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), is facing another looming crisis, with the supply of free medicines and essential items for patients at risk because of prolonged procurement delays, as reported by Dawn. According to Dawn, not a single tender at PIMS has been signed over the past six weeks, raising concerns that existing stocks of medicines and injectables could soon run out. A senior hospital official said the situation had worsened as procurement files continued to remain pending. Medicines and injections are provided free of charge to all indoor patients at PIMS, making uninterrupted procurement crucial for hospital operations. However, the absence of approved tenders has already disrupted supplies, while available stocks are reportedly declining rapidly. The latest crisis comes weeks after a fire at PIMS resulted in the deaths of 14 newborn babies on August 26. The additional charge of PIMS executive director was initially handed to National Institute of Health (NIH) chief Dr Mohammad Salman. However, he was removed on October 5, after which Prof Dr Tanwir Khaliq, vice chancellor of Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University (SZABMU), Islamabad, was given the additional responsibility. A senior doctor stated that procurement files were accumulating because they were awaiting signatures. The doctor also pointed to the limited involvement of purchase committee members, many of whom hold other departmental responsibilities, as highlighted by Dawn. A finance department official attributed part of the delay to administrative procedures involving the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). According to the official, changes in authorised signatories can take around two weeks to process, further slowing financial transactions and approvals. The official, however, said some stocks were still available and efforts were underway to resolve the matter, as reported by Dawn. (ANI)
